description: Container Image Linter for Security, Helping build the Best-Practice Docker Image, Easy to start

summary.one_liner: Dockle is a command-line linter that scans Docker/container images for security and best-practice problems, with checks based partly on CIS Benchmarks.
summary.what_it_does: Dockle inspects a container image (by name, or from a saved image tarball) and reports findings grouped under checkpoint codes such as CIS-DI-0001 and DKL-LI-0001, each at a level of FATAL, WARN, INFO, SKIP or PASS. Checks cover items like running as root, use of ADD instead of COPY, secrets in environment variables or files, HEALTHCHECK presence, setuid/setgid files, apt-get cache cleanup, the latest tag, and empty passwords. Output can be plain text, JSON, or SARIF, and can be written to a file. The tool can exit non-zero when WARN or FATAL alerts are found, which suits CI pipelines. Checkpoints can be ignored via flags, an environment variable, or a .dockleignore file, and accept/reject lists for env var names, filenames and extensions can be customized. The README says it can pull images from private registries (Docker Hub, Amazon ECR, GCR, and BasicAuth self-hosted registries) using environment variables.
use_cases: lint a Docker image for security issues before deploying
check container images for CIS Benchmark compliance
add image security checks to a CI pipeline
detect secrets or credential files baked into an image
enforce exit codes on image lint warnings
scan private registry images without installing Docker
notable: Checkpoint codes mapped to CIS Docker Benchmark items plus Dockle-specific checks
Scans images without needing Docker installed when pulling from registries (README states this)
Outputs JSON and SARIF for tooling integration
Ignore lists via flags, env var, or .dockleignore file
Accept and reject lists for suspicious env vars, filenames, and extensions
caveats: Requires Docker socket mounting to scan images on the host machine
By default exits with code 0 even when problems are found; a flag is needed for CI failure
Registry authentication relies on environment variables, which the README itself advises against on local machines
keywords: check docker image for root user
